notes: The metro (Zona Sul to Centro) is safe and clean; Uber and 99 are cheap; the Niterói ferry leaves from Praça XV. Galeão takes 45-60 minutes; Santos Dumont is in the city.

December to March is summer: 35-40°C, humid and rainy. Carnival falls in February or March (hotels cost three times as much, with blocos street parties). On New Year's Eve, 2 million people dress in white on Copacabana.

SAFETY: Don't show your phone on the street, don't leave belongings on the beach (swim one at a time), don't walk on the seafront at night, and don't enter a favela without a guide. Zona Sul (Ipanema, Leblon, Copacabana) is comfortable by day.

Corcovado train 100 BRL, Sugarloaf 180, Maracanã 60; por quilo (pay-by-weight) restaurant 40-60, chope 12, caipirinha 20; 10% service charge is added to the bill. Cards are accepted everywhere, and Pix works too.
Christ the Redeemer at 08:00 (cloud rolls in after noon), Sugarloaf at sunset; take the Ilha Grande tour early; Pedra Bonita in the morning.
Feijoada on Saturday, açaí, pão de queijo, moqueca, picanha; Globo biscuits on the beach.

stops.name: Christ the Redeemer Corcovado
stops.tips: The cog train from Cosme Velho (timed online tickets, first departure 08:00, about 100 BRL) climbs through Tijuca Forest. The 38 m Christ is quiet in the morning.

stops.name: Parque Lage
stops.tips: A mansion and pool courtyard beneath Corcovado, set in the forest. It was a location for a Snoop Dogg video.

stops.name: Santa Teresa Bar do Mineiro
stops.tips: A bohemian hilltop neighbourhood. Try feijoada (Saturday) and bolinho (fried snack), and ride the tram (bonde).

stops.name: Escadaria Selarón
stops.tips: 2,000 tiled steps by a Chilean artist, leading down to Lapa. There are Turkish tiles among them too.

stops.name: Arcos da Lapa
stops.tips: An aqueduct from 1750. Samba at night (Fridays at Rio Scenarium).

backups.name: Aprazível Santa Teresa
backups.tips: A forest restaurant with treehouse-style dining. Views over Guanabara Bay; book ahead.

backups.name: Museu Chácara do Céu
backups.tips: A modern art villa in Santa Teresa, with views.

stops.name: Copacabana Beach
stops.tips: Winter (Jun-Sep) is sunny at 24°C, which locals say is the best season. The sea is 22°C.

stops.name: Arpoador Rock
stops.tips: A rock between Copacabana and Ipanema, with surfers and views of Dois Irmãos.

stops.name: Ipanema Beach Posto 9
stops.tips: The beach of The Girl from Ipanema. Vendors sell biscoito Globo (light crunchy biscuits) and mate; Posto 9 has a young crowd.

stops.name: Garota de Ipanema Bar
stops.tips: The bar where the song was written. Order picanha (grilled beef) and chope (draught beer).

stops.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
stops.tips: A two-stage cable car (Urca 220 m, Sugarloaf 396 m). Go for sunset and the city lights at night; timed online tickets.

backups.name: Bar Urca
backups.tips: Beer and pastel (fried pastry) on the Urca sea wall. A local classic, before the cable car.

backups.name: Forte de Copacabana
backups.tips: A fort at the end of the beach, with the Confeitaria Colombo café. An alternative to Arpoador.

stops.name: Museum of Tomorrow
stops.tips: Calatrava's Museum of Tomorrow on the Porto Maravilha waterfront. Free on Tuesdays.

stops.name: Monastery of São Bento
stops.tips: A gold-covered Baroque monastery from 1590. Gregorian mass on Sundays at 10:00.

stops.name: Confeitaria Colombo
stops.tips: A Belle Époque pastry shop from 1894. Mirrored hall, pastel de nata and salgados (savoury snacks).

stops.name: Real Gabinete Português de Leitura
stops.tips: One of the world's most beautiful libraries (Neo-Manueline style). Free.

stops.name: Pedra do Sal
stops.tips: The rock where samba was born. Street roda (samba circle) on Mondays and Fridays; try a caipirinha.

backups.name: Rio Scenarium
backups.tips: A three-storey samba house packed with antiques. Fridays and Saturdays.

backups.name: Theatro Municipal
backups.tips: A replica of the Paris Opera. Check tour times.

stops.name: Pedra Bonita Trail
stops.tips: 693 m in Tijuca. An easy 40-minute climb to a hang-gliding ramp, with views of Pedra da Gávea and São Conrado.

stops.name: Cascatinha Taunay Tijuca Forest
stops.tips: A 30 m waterfall in the world's largest urban forest. Look out for monkeys; take an Uber or taxi.

stops.name: Dona Marta Viewpoint
stops.tips: The most famous frame of Christ, Sugarloaf and the bay. A Michael Jackson video was shot here.

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden
stops.tips: A botanical garden from 1808. A 134 m avenue of imperial palms and Vitória Régia giant water lilies.

stops.name: Braseiro da Gávea
stops.tips: Picanha and chope in Gávea. A meat restaurant popular with locals.

backups.name: Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas Cycling
backups.tips: A 7.5 km loop around the lagoon, with boats. An alternative to the botanical garden.

backups.name: Bar Lagoa
backups.tips: A German-Brazilian bar on the lagoon shore, open since 1934.

stops.name: Conceição de Jacareí Ilha Grande Boat
stops.tips: A 2.5-hour transfer from Rio plus a 20-minute boat ride (tour about 250 BRL). A car-free forest island.

stops.name: Vila do Abraão
stops.tips: The island's village, with sandy streets and a church.

stops.name: Lopes Mendes Beach
stops.tips: One of Brazil's most beautiful beaches. Take a boat plus a 20-minute forest walk; white sand and bodyboarding.

stops.name: Lua e Mar Beach Tavern Abraão
stops.tips: Moqueca (fish stew) and caipirinha. The return boat leaves at 16:30.

backups.name: Lagoa Azul Snorkelling Tour
backups.tips: A boat tour to the Blue Lagoon with turtles and fish. An alternative to Lopes Mendes.

backups.name: Praia do Abraãozinho Kiosk
backups.tips: A cove beach next to the village.

stops.name: Niterói Contemporary Art Museum
stops.tips: Niemeyer's flying saucer. The ferry takes 20 minutes (from Praça XV), and it has the best view of the Rio skyline.

stops.name: Parque da Cidade Niterói
stops.tips: A hilltop in Niterói with a bay panorama stretching to Christ the Redeemer, and hang-gliding.

stops.name: Itacoatiara Beach
stops.tips: Watch the winter surf. Beach kiosks.

stops.name: Mercado São Pedro Niterói
stops.tips: Upstairs restaurants above the fish market. Fried fish.

stops.name: Maracanã Stadium Tour
stops.tips: The world's legendary stadium. Take a tour or catch a match (Flamengo or Fluminense, a real experience!); get there by metro.

backups.name: Flamengo Match Maracanã
backups.tips: A match-day stand. The best Rio experience; buy tickets online.

backups.name: Skunna Niterói
backups.tips: A seafront restaurant in Niterói, with views.

stops.name: Mirante do Leblon
stops.tips: A lookout at the end of Leblon, with views of the Ipanema and Leblon beaches and Dois Irmãos.

stops.name: Leblon Beach Morning
stops.tips: Rio's most elegant beach. Have coconut water (água de coco).

stops.name: Talho Capixaba Leblon
stops.tips: A Leblon bakery-deli breakfast. Pão de queijo (cheese bread) for your farewell.

stops.name: Feira Hippie Ipanema
stops.tips: A handicrafts market on Sundays at Praça General Osório (on other days, visit a Havaianas store).

stops.name: Galeão Airport Uber
stops.tips: Uber takes 45-60 minutes. Farewell.

backups.name: Bibi Sucos Leblon
backups.tips: A cult spot for açaí and fruit juice.
